featured_reviews.name: alisha khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience with Shapoorji Pallonji Joyville Virar. I decided to go with them for my project and paid a token amount, expecting professionalism and reliability. Unfortunately, I was met with poor communication and delays. When I requested a refund of my token amount due to these issues, they were unresponsive and refused to process my request. It’s frustrating to deal with a builder who does not honor their commitments. I would not recommend Shapoorji Pallonji Joyville Virar to anyone looking for a trustworthy partner in their construction project.

I do not want to name but I have to because these people were nightmare for me.

Mithilesh Kumar, Nitesh Dubey, Vikash Mathur and Hanuman they all are included in this scam so I would recommend not to get scammed by these people. They are just at the site to scam people in the name of a brand.

Shapoorji Pallonji is a great brand but people working for it are making it worst.

I paid 51,000 INR as a token amount and they said I will get it back if I face any issues in future but later on denied for it when I came to know about their false promises stating that their policy does not allow to refund token amount.

I would suggest everyone to first do proper research and read all the papers and also get everything in writing from them because later on they lie about the promises that they make so it is better to take everything in writing.

I also feel that they got few papers signed from me by mixing those papers with other papers which I was not aware of. I seriously don't know how they did this but they scammed me.

I lost my hard earned money so please DO NOT GET SCAMMED BY THESE SCAMMERS.

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Do read before buying extremely disappointing and feels like a deliberate fraud. Misleading

False assurances: They verbally convinced me that my building would be ready by March 2026, but insisted on writing 2028 in the agreement, claiming the entire cluster of buildings would take that long. Their line was: “Don’t worry, your specific building will be ready by 2026, but we must mention 2028 on paper for the whole project.” This is how buyers are trapped — verbal promises vs. written reality.

Bank disbursement trap: ICICI Bank was convinced by Mayfair’s claim that the project was “80% completed” and released 90% of the loan amount. The shocking part is that buyers trust the bank’s scrutiny, assuming such a strong institution must have verified progress. In reality, banks rely only on builder‑issued certificates, not actual site inspections. Since November, the project has remained stuck at “80% completion” with no visible progress.

Unfinished yet expanding: The funniest and most frustrating part is that their existing buildings are not even complete, yet they are already starting new sites in the same location. Buyers don’t question this, and that silence is exactly how they get trapped.

Buyer deception: This is the biggest fraud — lure buyers with optimistic verbal timelines, get them to sign papers, and later hide behind the written agreement that pushes delivery years ahead.

I strongly caution anyone considering Mayfair projects: do not trust verbal commitments, rely only on the written agreement. Be vigilant with loan disbursements, because once banks release funds, you are left paying EMIs while waiting years for possession.

featured_reviews.name: Sujata Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
The builder of Mayfair Virar Garden has truly deceived us. If you plan to live in this building, you must learn to live without water, just like people did in ancient villages — although, back then, even villages had better access to water than we do here. The situation is extremely poor; neither do they provide regular water supply nor is any of their maintenance work done properly.

It has been two months since our bathroom door broke, and despite repeated requests, no repairs have been made. We moved in with great passion and hope, but even basic issues are ignored. Their staff member Sangram does not have the patience to listen — he only argues his own point and shows no concern for residents’ problems. The entire staff seems to have only one line of defense: “What can we do? We are helpless.”They provide Samgram no as emergency on board but funniest think is that he is not received your single call any time.

For the past three days, our water tanks haven’t filled up. It almost seems like the Mayfair builder has some kind of arrangement with VVCMC, as the municipal water supply is stopped four days a week only for this building — as if the builder himself grants holidays to the water department.

If you genuinely wish to buy a home where you can live peacefully, please do not buy here. There are many good builders in Virar — such as Yashwant and Bachraj — who actually deliver on their promises. We were dreaming of our home of dreams, but unfortunately, it remains just that — a dream. In reality, living here without water is worse than living in a remote villllage. This builder is not professional at all — they only care about their business and are experts at misleading and fooling people.
